title: Delete config.py and its tests; drop pydantic and pyyaml
description:
Remove src/paddock/config.py and tests/test_config.py. Drop pydantic and pyyaml from pyproject.toml dependencies (typer remains) and regenerate uv.lock. Remove paths.settings_path().

This deletes the Settings model, the single-file loader, resolve_environment (including the `{command: ...}` shell-resolution feature used for pulling secrets out of 1Password/aws-cli), and ca_certificate_paths validation. Env vars now reach the container three ways, none of which paddock parses: the user's shell (via the compose file's valueless pass-through entries), a .env the user writes in the config dir, or an env/env_file stanza in their override compose. CA certs are now detected as *.crt files in the config dir, not listed in YAML — see the paths and compose-driver tasks.

Note the capability being consciously given up: with no resolve_environment, secrets can no longer be pulled from a command at `up` time by paddock itself. The equivalent is now the user's own shell (`GITHUB_TOKEN=$(op read ...) paddock up`) or a generated .env. Call this out in the README so it does not look like an oversight.
acceptance_criteria:
- pyproject dependencies list contains typer only
- uv.lock regenerated and committed; `uv sync` clean
- No import of pydantic or yaml anywhere in src/ or tests/
notes: milhouse iteration 1 ended error: could not start the agent: herdr agent start failed: `herdr agent start milhouse-paddock-96h.2 --kind claude --pane wM:p1 --timeout 60000` exited 1: {"error":{"code":"invalid_agent_name","message":"agent name must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits, '-' or '_' (1-32 characters)"},"id":"cli:agent:start"}

title: Rework paths.py around the config directory contract
description:
paths.py becomes the single place that knows the config-dir layout and the packaged-image location.

Keep: config_dir() -> ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/paddock.

Add:
- compose_file() -> the packaged src/paddock/image/docker-compose.yml (importlib-based, resolved off __file__ like container.IMAGE_DIR does today)
- override_file() -> config_dir()/docker-compose.override.yml
- env_file() -> config_dir()/.env
- authorized_keys_path() -> config_dir()/authorized_keys
- certs_dir() -> config_dir()/certs

Drop: settings_path(), state_dir(), ssh_home_dir(). paddock no longer keeps any state of its own — docker owns all of it now (images, containers, volumes), which is worth stating in AGENTS.md since 'no XDG state dir' is a deliberate property, not an omission.

These are path predicates only. Existence checks and error messages belong in the CLI/preflight task.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every path helper is exercised by a test against a tmp_path XDG_CONFIG_HOME
- No state-dir helper remains; tests/conftest.py stops setting XDG_STATE_HOME

title: Add compose.py: the docker compose invocation and interpolation environment
description:
New module replacing container.py. It owns two pure functions plus a thin runner, so the interesting logic is testable without a docker daemon.

compose_args(subcommand_args) -> list[str]:
  docker compose -f <packaged compose file> [-f <override> if it exists] [--env-file <config .env> if it exists] <subcommand_args...>
  Order matters: the packaged file first (it establishes the project directory), the override second so it wins.

interpolation_env(refresh_tools: bool) -> dict[str, str]:
  Starts from os.environ (so the compose file's valueless pass-through entries still pick up the user's shell) and layers on:
  - PADDOCK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS: always set, to the config-dir path, whether or not it exists
  - PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT: set to config_dir()/certs only when that directory contains at least one *.crt; otherwise left unset so the compose default (./ca-certificates, shipped empty) applies
  - PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH: a fresh unix timestamp when refresh_tools, otherwise left unset so the compose default of 0 reuses the cache
  Never overwrite a variable the user already set in their own environment except where that is the whole point (PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH on an explicit `build`); in particular PADDOCK_SSH_PORT/PADDOCK_HTTP_PORT are pass-through only, paddock does not set them.

run(args, env) -> None and exec_(args, env) for the passthrough case, raising a typed ComposeError on non-zero exit or a missing docker executable, in keeping with the existing per-layer exception convention (ConfigError/DockerError/SshError -> now just ComposeError, handled only in cli.py).

Note for the --env-file semantics: compose's --env-file feeds *interpolation* (so it is the right lever for PADDOCK_SSH_PORT and friends), and is not by itself a way to inject arbitrary env into the container. Container env belongs in the compose file's environment/env_file. Get this distinction into the docstring so the README can be accurate about it.
design: Why interpolation vars rather than a generated file: the compose project directory is inside site-packages and must stay read-only, so there is nowhere project-local to write a .env. Setting variables in the child process environment sidesteps that entirely and leaves no state on disk.
acceptance_criteria:
- compose_args builds both -f flags only when the override exists, verified by test
- interpolation_env omits PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT when certs/ is absent or has no *.crt, and sets it when it does
- interpolation_env leaves PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH unset unless refresh was asked for
- ComposeError raised (not a traceback) when docker is missing or exits non-zero

title: Rebuild cli.py as typer subcommands over compose
description:
Replace the single mutually-exclusive-flags command with real subcommands. There is no longer a default action: bare `paddock` prints help.

- build [--cached] [--no-cache]: compose build. Fresh PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH by default so claude/copilot/codex/herdr/bd reinstall latest; --cached pins it to 0; --no-cache passes through to compose for a full rebuild. This replaces the `agent-up` alias agent-container's README asked users to define.
- up [--build] [--cached]: compose up -d (always detached — there is no attach story anymore, so a foreground up would just be a log tail with a confusing Ctrl-C). An implicit build here stays cached unless --build is combined with the refresh default.
- down [--volumes]: compose down; --volumes forwards -v and must be explicit, since that destroys agent_home (tool auth, shell history, dotfiles).
- start / stop / restart: the corresponding compose subcommands.
- status: compose ps. Include the resolved published ssh port in the output, since that is the one thing a user needs in order to connect and paddock no longer connects for them.
- logs [-f]: compose logs.
- compose: passthrough, exec-ing docker compose with the same -f/--env-file/env assembly plus whatever the user passed (e.g. `paddock compose -- exec agent zsh`). This is the escape hatch that keeps the wrapper from needing to grow a subcommand per compose verb.
- --version stays as an eager callback.

Keep the existing error-handling convention: lower layers raise, cli.py catches ComposeError and calls _fail, which prints a red `error:` to stderr and raises typer.Exit(1).
acceptance_criteria:
- `paddock --help` lists every subcommand; bare `paddock` exits 0 with help
- `paddock status` reports the published ssh port
- `paddock compose -- config` renders the merged compose file
- `paddock down --volumes` is the only path that can remove volumes

title: Delete ssh.py and its tests; drop herdr and ssh-keygen from the dependency check
description:
Remove src/paddock/ssh.py and tests/test_ssh.py entirely, along with paths.state_dir()/ssh_home_dir() and everything in cli.py that calls into them.

What goes away, and is not replaced anywhere: the dedicated ed25519 keypair generation, the isolated $HOME used for the herdr subprocess (and the two hard-won gotchas that came with it — ssh's tilde expansion resolving against the passwd database rather than $HOME, and IdentitiesOnly being needed so a forwarded agent cannot exhaust MaxAuthTries), the HERDR_CONFIG_PATH plumbing, and the os.execvpe into herdr.

REQUIRED_EXECUTABLES drops to docker alone. Nothing in paddock cares whether herdr or ssh-keygen exists on the host anymore — herdr is still installed *inside* the image, and connecting is the user's business.

Keep the removed ssh-home rationale reachable in git history rather than re-explaining it in the new docs; AGENTS.md should just stop describing ssh.py.
acceptance_criteria:
- No reference to herdr, ssh-keygen, ssh_home, or HERDR_CONFIG_PATH anywhere under src/ or tests/
- `uv run pytest` passes with test_ssh.py gone

title: Validate additional_contexts + COPY --from against the local docker/compose version
description:
Spike, ahead of committing to the CA design. `build.additional_contexts` needs a reasonably current Compose (v2.17+) and a buildx-backed build; `COPY --from=<named context>` needs BuildKit. Confirm on the actual machines paddock runs on (including Colima, if that is still the Mac setup) that:

- `docker compose build` picks up additional_contexts without an explicit DOCKER_BUILDKIT/buildx opt-in
- a named context pointing at an absolute path outside the project directory is accepted
- an empty named-context directory does not fail the COPY

If any of that does not hold, fall back to the staged-temp-build-context approach for builds only (paddock 2.x's container.py already did exactly this: copy the packaged image dir plus configured certs into a temp dir and build there), while up/down/logs keep running -f from the package dir. Record which way it went in the epic's design notes, since the compose file and Dockerfile both depend on the answer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Documented `docker compose version` / buildx version this was verified against
- A build with a cert in ~/.config/paddock/certs/ demonstrably trusts it inside the container (curl against a proxied host, or openssl verify against the merged bundle)
- Decision recorded on the epic
notes:
BLOCKED ON A HOST RUN. The dev environment for this repo is the paddock
container itself: no docker binary, no /var/run/docker.sock, and no daemon on
host.docker.internal:2375/2376 (host.docker.internal resolves to 192.168.5.2,
i.e. a Colima/lima gateway). The empirical part of this spike cannot run from
inside the container and has to be executed on the host(s).

Harness written and smoke-tested: spike-additional-contexts.sh. It builds
throwaway images against debian:trixie-slim (override with BASE_IMAGE=),
removes them on exit, and touches nothing under ~/.config/paddock. It always
invokes compose the way paddock will (absolute -f, from a cwd that is NOT the
project dir) and unsets DOCKER_BUILDKIT/COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD/COMPOSE_BAKE
first, so the no-opt-in question is actually tested.

Checks:
 2.  relative default ./ca-certificates (holding only .gitkeep) is honored,
     and resolves against the compose file's dir rather than cwd
 2b. same build with '# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1' pinned
 3.  a truly empty named-context dir does not break COPY
 4.  an absolute path outside the project dir is accepted
 5.  end-to-end trust: a leaf signed by a CA in certs/ verifies against
     /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt inside the image, WITH a control that
     the same leaf fails against the no-extra-CA image
 6.  informational: nonexistent context dir, and forced DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0

It prints a paste-ready SUMMARY with versions and one of three verdicts:
GO / GO-but-pin-the-syntax-directive / NO-GO-fall-back-to-staged-temp-context.

Why 2b exists: COPY --from=<named context> needs dockerfile frontend >= 1.4.
Without testing both variants a failure is ambiguous between "additional_contexts
is unusable here" and "the built-in frontend is old, add one line". Expected
floors, to be CONFIRMED by the run, not treated as established:
  - build.additional_contexts -> Compose v2.17.0+
  - buildx --build-context    -> buildx v0.8.0+
  - COPY --from=<ctx>         -> dockerfile frontend 1.4+

Validated locally without docker: the cert fixture logic is sound (real
openssl) — CA is basicConstraints CA:TRUE, leaf verifies against the CA,
fails against the plain system bundle, passes against the bundle with the CA
appended. So check 5 measures what it claims to. The leaf is deliberately kept
OUT of certs/, or update-ca-certificates would trust the leaf itself and the
check would pass for the wrong reason.

NEXT: run on the Mac/Colima host and on any Linux host, paste both SUMMARY
blocks here, then record the decision on the epic (paddock-aye) design notes.
aye.1 and aye.2 stay blocked until then.
close_reason: GO: additional_contexts + COPY --from=<named context> verified working on macOS/Colima (docker server 27.4.0, compose 5.3.1, buildx v0.36.0) with no BuildKit opt-in. All six checks passed including end-to-end CA trust with a negative control. Staged-temp-build-context fallback not needed. Decision recorded on the paddock-aye epic design; implementation consequences recorded on aye.1 and aye.2.

title: Rewrite the paddock Python layer as a docker compose wrapper
description:
Strip paddock down to container lifecycle management. Delete the ssh/herdr attach layer and the settings.yaml config layer, and replace container.py's hand-rolled `docker run` wrappers with a thin docker-compose driver plus a typer subcommand surface.

paddock's whole job after this: assemble the right `docker compose` invocation (packaged base file + optional per-machine override, plus the PADDOCK_* interpolation variables), validate the surrounding config before handing off, and surface errors cleanly. Connecting to the container (herdr, ssh) is the user's business and paddock no longer touches it.
design:
Decisions already made:
- CLI is subcommands, not flags: build, up, down, start, stop, restart, status, logs, and `paddock compose -- <args>` passthrough for anything unwrapped. No default/bare action that attaches.
- ssh.py is deleted outright. No keypair generation, no isolated ssh home, no ssh_config emission, no herdr exec. The user writes ~/.config/paddock/authorized_keys themselves and connects however they like.
- config.py is deleted outright. pydantic and pyyaml come off the dependency list. Env vars for the container come from the user's shell, their own .env, or their override compose file.
- `paddock build` busts the TOOLS_REFRESH cache gate by default (fresh timestamp, so claude/copilot/codex/herdr/bd track latest); --cached reuses it. An implicit build during `up` stays cached (TOOLS_REFRESH unset -> 0).
- Only docker (and its compose plugin) is a required executable now.
acceptance_criteria:
- src/paddock/ contains cli.py, compose.py, paths.py, __init__.py, image/ — no ssh.py, no config.py, no container.py
- pyproject dependencies are typer only; uv.lock regenerated
- Every subcommand shells out to docker compose with both -f flags (override only when the file exists) and the PADDOCK_* variables set
- `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ty check` all clean

title: Vendor the agent-container image and compose file into paddock
description:
paddock becomes the home of the container image. Copy agent-container's Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, entrypoint.sh, and sshd_config into src/paddock/image/ as the source of truth, reconciling them with the fixes paddock's own copy already carries, and parameterize the compose file so per-machine config (port, CA certs, authorized_keys, tool-refresh) is driven by environment interpolation rather than by editing files inside the installed package.

Source of truth for the vendored files: /home/agent/code/github.com/kris-steinhoff/agent-container (its Dockerfile is ahead of paddock's copy). agent-container is retired afterward.
design:
Decisions already made:
- Vendor into src/paddock/image/ (agent-container repo is retired, not kept in sync).
- Compose runs with -f pointed straight at the packaged file, so the compose project directory IS the installed package directory. Nothing may write into it at runtime, and every relative path in the compose file resolves against it.
- Per-machine input therefore arrives as compose interpolation variables that paddock sets in the child process environment (PADDOCK_*), plus an optional ~/.config/paddock/docker-compose.override.yml layered with a second -f.
- Config dir (~/.config/paddock, XDG-respecting) holds: authorized_keys, certs/*.crt, docker-compose.override.yml, and an optional .env.
- No settings.yaml. No paddock-side YAML parsing at all.

CA DELIVERY: GO on build.additional_contexts (settled by paddock-aye.6).
Verified 2026-07-30 on macOS 15 / Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 under Colima:
docker client 29.6.2, docker SERVER 27.4.0 (the server is what matters, it
carries the BuildKit that resolves the named context), compose 5.3.1,
buildx v0.36.0, context+builder "colima" on the docker driver. Not yet
re-verified on a Linux host, no such machine was exercised.

So the compose file carries:
    build:
      context: .
      additional_contexts:
        ca-certificates: ${PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT:-./ca-certificates}
and the Dockerfile carries:
    COPY --from=ca-certificates . /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/paddock/
    RUN update-ca-certificates

Confirmed empirically, not assumed:
- additional_contexts is honored by `docker compose build` with NO
  DOCKER_BUILDKIT / COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD / buildx opt-in.
- A relative named-context value resolves against the compose FILE's
  directory, not the caller's cwd. This is what makes `-f <package>/…` from
  an arbitrary cwd safe, and it is the whole reason the packaged default
  works without paddock computing an absolute path.
- An absolute path outside the project directory is accepted, so
  ~/.config/paddock/certs can be handed over as-is. Under Colima the context
  is streamed over the API, so the path does NOT need to be inside a
  directory shared into the VM.
- A truly empty named-context directory does not break the COPY, and a
  non-.crt file (.gitkeep) in the drop directory does not upset
  update-ca-certificates.
- No `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` directive is required: the built-in
  frontend on server 27.4.0 is already >= 1.4. The pinned-frontend variant
  also passes, so adding the directive stays available as a compatibility
  lever if an older machine ever shows up.
- End to end: a CA dropped in certs/ is trusted inside the built image (a
  leaf signed by it verifies against /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt),
  and the same leaf fails against an image built without the CA.

The staged-temp-build-context fallback (paddock 2.x container.py build())
is therefore NOT needed and should not be carried forward. Builds and
up/down/logs all run -f straight from the package dir.

Two consequences for the implementation, recorded on aye.2:
- A named context pointing at a nonexistent directory is a hard build
  failure ("failed to get build context ca-certificates: stat …: no such
  file or directory"). paddock must only export PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT when the
  config certs dir actually exists, and otherwise leave the compose default
  to point at the packaged ca-certificates/.
- DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 exported in the user's shell breaks the build. paddock
  should neutralize it in the compose child environment or fail clearly.
acceptance_criteria:
- src/paddock/image/ contains Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, entrypoint.sh, sshd_config, ca-certificates/.gitkeep
- `docker compose -f src/paddock/image/docker-compose.yml build` succeeds from a clean cache with no config dir present
- The built image contains claude, codex, copilot, opencode, bd, terraform, herdr, nvim, gh, glab, uv, chezmoi
- sshd accepts a key from a config-dir authorized_keys after `up`

title: Vendor the Dockerfile, reconciling agent-container's version with paddock's fixes
description:
Copy agent-container's Dockerfile over src/paddock/image/Dockerfile, then re-apply the fixes paddock's copy already has. The two have diverged in both directions.

Take from agent-container (paddock's copy lacks these):
- apt packages: jq, bubblewrap, python3-venv, python3-pip
- the terraform install step
- the TOOLS_REFRESH cache gate near the bottom, and everything below it: herdr, @github/copilot, @openai/codex, and the beads (bd) installer
- claude-code moved below the gate (paddock's copy installs it above, in the cached npm layer)

Keep from paddock's copy (agent-container lacks these):
- the wider CA env var set: SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, GIT_SSL_CAINFO alongside NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, PIP_CERT, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
- sshd_config baked to /etc/paddock/sshd_config instead of straight into /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ (agent-container has a latent bug here: /etc/ssh is a named volume, and Docker only seeds a named volume from the image on first use, so a config file written under /etc/ssh by the image is silently never updated by a later rebuild)
- the ~/.zshrc removal comment that reflects why the file is actually there (/etc/skel from Debian's zsh package), not the uv-installer explanation

New in this task:
- replace `COPY certs/ /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/extra/` with `COPY --from=ca-certificates . /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/paddock/`, fed by the compose file's additional_contexts (see the compose task)
- rename the /run mount path referenced anywhere from agent-container to paddock
design: COPY --from=<named context> needs BuildKit/buildx, which `docker compose build` uses by default in compose v2. The named context is always defined (it defaults to a ./ca-certificates dir shipped empty in the package), so the COPY never fails for a missing source — same property the current temp-build-context approach has.
acceptance_criteria:
- Clean-cache build succeeds with no config dir present
- Build succeeds with a real *.crt in ~/.config/paddock/certs/ and update-ca-certificates reports it added
- Changing PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH rebuilds only the layers below the gate
notes:
From the paddock-aye.6 spike (GO on additional_contexts). The CA block
becomes:
    COPY --from=ca-certificates . /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/paddock/
    RUN update-ca-certificates
replacing 2.x's `COPY ca-certificates/ ...` from a staged temp context.

No `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` directive is needed: the built-in frontend
on docker server 27.4.0 is already >= 1.4 and the bare Dockerfile passed.
The pinned-frontend variant also passed, so the directive is available as a
compatibility lever if an older machine turns up, at the cost of a registry
pull for the frontend image.

A non-.crt file in the drop directory (the shipped .gitkeep) does not upset
update-ca-certificates, so the packaged empty ca-certificates/ is safe as
the default context.

title: Vendor and parameterize docker-compose.yml
description:
Copy agent-container's docker-compose.yml to src/paddock/image/docker-compose.yml and replace every path/port that assumed a hand-edited repo checkout with an interpolation variable, since the file now lives read-only inside site-packages.

Shape to land on:
- `name: paddock`, one service `agent`, `image: paddock`
- ports: `127.0.0.1:${PADDOCK_SSH_PORT:-2222}:22` and `127.0.0.1:${PADDOCK_HTTP_PORT:-8000}:8000` — 2222 is the default, overridable via the environment (either the user's shell or the config-dir .env)
- build.args: `TOOLS_REFRESH: ${PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH:-0}`
- build.additional_contexts: `ca-certificates: ${PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT:-./ca-certificates}` — the relative default resolves against the package dir, where an empty ca-certificates/ ships
- volumes: `${PADDOCK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS}:/run/paddock/authorized_keys:ro`, plus named volumes `agent_home:/home/agent` and `sshd_host_keys:/etc/ssh`
- extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway (kept from agent-container, for Colima and for reaching a host-local model server)
- environment pass-through list: GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (valueless entries, resolved from paddock's own environment; anything else goes in the user's override)
- restart: unless-stopped (paddock 2.x set this on `docker run`; agent-container's compose didn't)

Deliberately NOT in this file: the commented-out project bind mount example from agent-container. That is now the primary job of the per-machine override compose, and belongs in the README's override example instead.
design:
Volume keys are named `agent_home` and `sshd_host_keys` so the project prefix yields paddock_agent_home / paddock_sshd_host_keys. Note the near-miss: paddock 2.x created paddock_ssh_host_keys imperatively, and compose refuses to adopt a pre-existing volume it did not label as its own — so `sshd_host_keys` (not `ssh_host_keys`) is what keeps a stale 2.x volume from colliding with the new project. Reusing an existing volume is still possible on purpose, via external: true in the override compose (covered in the migration task).

The authorized_keys mount is unconditional, and compose cannot express a conditional mount. paddock always sets PADDOCK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS (so interpolation never produces a malformed `:/run/...` mount spec) and separately validates that the file exists before commands that start the container — otherwise Docker would helpfully create a *directory* at that path and sshd would come up with no usable key.
acceptance_criteria:
- `docker compose -f src/paddock/image/docker-compose.yml config` renders with only PADDOCK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS set
- Overriding PADDOCK_SSH_PORT changes the published port; unset yields 2222
- An override file layered with a second -f can add a bind mount and extra env without touching the base file
notes:
From the paddock-aye.6 spike (GO on additional_contexts). Two things the
compose file and the Python wrapper have to get right:

1. Never point a named context at a path that might not exist. A missing
   directory is a hard build failure:
     failed to get build context ca-certificates: stat <path>: no such file
     or directory
   So the compose file keeps the packaged fallback:
     ca-certificates: ${PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT:-./ca-certificates}
   and paddock only exports PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT when the config certs dir
   actually exists. Do NOT export it unconditionally, and do NOT mkdir into
   ~/.config/paddock just to satisfy the build.

2. DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 in the user's shell breaks the build (confirmed). The
   compose child environment should neutralize it, or the failure needs a
   clear paddock-level error rather than a raw buildx one.

Also confirmed and relied on: a RELATIVE additional_contexts value resolves
against the compose file's directory, not the caller's cwd. That is what
makes the packaged default work without paddock computing an absolute path.

title: Version bump, quality gates, and a real end-to-end pass
description:
Bump to 3.0 in pyproject.toml (the CLI surface, the config format, and the volume names all break compatibility with 2.0).

Run the gates: uv run ruff format ., uv run ruff check ., uv run ty check, uv run pytest.

Then an actual end-to-end run, since none of the docker-facing code is unit-tested by design and the whole point of this refactor is the docker path:
- clean slate (no config dir, no volumes): paddock build, write authorized_keys, paddock up, ssh in, confirm claude/codex/bd/nvim/terraform are present
- paddock status shows the port; paddock logs works; paddock compose -- exec agent zsh gets a shell
- paddock stop / start / restart round-trip with the container keeping its host key (no known_hosts churn)
- rebuild the image and confirm the sshd_config.d/paddock.conf refresh still happens against the pre-existing host-keys volume
- an override compose adding a project bind mount takes effect
- paddock down leaves volumes; paddock down --volumes removes them
acceptance_criteria:
- All four gates clean
- Every bullet above performed and any surprises filed as new issues
- Version reads 3.0 and `paddock --version` agrees

title: Rewrite README for the compose-based, connection-agnostic paddock
description:
The current README is wrong in its first paragraph (it says paddock attaches with herdr) and describes a settings.yaml that no longer exists. Rewrite around:

- What paddock is now: it builds and runs one general-purpose dev container via docker compose, and nothing else. Connecting is up to you — the image still ships herdr and sshd, so `herdr --remote ssh://agent@localhost:2222` is the intended path, but paddock does not run it and does not manage your ssh config or keys.
- Install (uv tool install), and the docker + compose-plugin requirement.
- The subcommand reference.
- The config directory: authorized_keys (required, with the `ssh-add -L` recipe for agent-held keys), certs/*.crt, docker-compose.override.yml, .env.
- Every PADDOCK_* variable, what reads it, and its default: PADDOCK_SSH_PORT (2222), PADDOCK_HTTP_PORT (8000), PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT, PADDOCK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS, PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH.
- Env vars and secrets: the three routes (shell, config-dir .env, override compose) and the explicit note that paddock no longer resolves secrets from commands the way settings.yaml's `{command: ...}` did — `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(op read ...) paddock up` is the replacement. Also be precise that --env-file drives compose interpolation while container env comes from the compose file's environment/env_file.
- Persistence: paddock_agent_home and paddock_sshd_host_keys, what survives what, and that down --volumes is the destructive one.
- The tools cache gate: `paddock build` refreshes the fast-moving tools by default, --cached does not.
acceptance_criteria:
- No claim that paddock attaches, generates keys, or reads settings.yaml
- Every PADDOCK_* variable documented with its default
- The dropped {command: ...} secret resolution is explicitly addressed rather than silently missing

title: Update AGENTS.md for the new module layout and invariants
description:
AGENTS.md currently documents paths/config/container/ssh/cli and several gotchas that are about to be either deleted or relocated. Rewrite its Architecture, Commands, and Testing sections for: paths.py (config-dir contract, and the deliberate absence of any paddock state dir), compose.py (argv + interpolation env, why variables rather than a generated file), cli.py (subcommands, ComposeError as the only typed exception left), and image/ (vendored from the retired agent-container).

Gotchas worth carrying forward, because they are all still live and all cost real debugging time:
- /etc/ssh is a named volume, Docker seeds a named volume from the image only on first use, so sshd config must be baked outside /etc/ssh and copied in by entrypoint.sh on every start.
- The compose project directory is inside site-packages and must stay read-only: that is why per-machine input is interpolation variables, and why every relative path in the compose file resolves against the package dir.
- Compose will not adopt a pre-existing named volume it did not label, which is why the host-keys volume key was renamed away from paddock 2.x's paddock_ssh_host_keys.
- The authorized_keys mount cannot be conditional in compose, so a missing file must be caught by preflight or Docker silently creates a directory there.

Gotchas to delete along with their code: the ssh tilde-expansion-vs-$HOME trap, IdentitiesOnly/MaxAuthTries, and the ~/.ssh/environment refresh trick (including the reason cli.py's default path unconditionally called _start()).

Keep the error-handling-convention and dependency-policy sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- No section describes ssh.py, config.py, container.py, or settings.yaml
- The four live gotchas above are present
- Commands section matches the actual subcommands

title: Write the migration path off agent-container and paddock 2.x
description:
Two migrations, both of which risk quietly losing a volume full of tool auth and shell history.

From agent-container: its compose project was named agent-container, so its volumes are agent-container_agent_home and agent-container_ssh_host_keys. Document reusing the home volume rather than starting over, via the override compose — this is a good motivating example for the override mechanism generally:

  volumes:
    agent_home:
      external: true
      name: agent-container_agent_home

Also cover: stop and remove the old stack, and the `Include ~/.config/.../ssh_config` line in ~/.ssh/config that agent-container's README told users to add (paddock no longer ships an ssh_config, so that Include either needs repointing at a hand-written host block or removing — a dangling Include is a silent ssh config error).

From paddock 2.x: the imperative container/image named paddock and volumes paddock_home / paddock_ssh_host_keys. `docker rm -f paddock` and `docker volume rm paddock_home paddock_ssh_host_keys` after salvaging anything wanted, and note that compose would have refused to adopt the old host-keys volume anyway.

Port collision: if an old stack is still on 2222, PADDOCK_SSH_PORT is how the two coexist during the transition.
acceptance_criteria:
- Documented external-volume override that demonstrably starts with an existing agent-container home volume
- Cleanup commands for both old stacks, with the destructive ones called out
- The dangling ssh_config Include is addressed

title: Test the compose argv and environment assembly
description:
Keep the existing testing posture: pure logic only, no docker daemon. What used to be covered (config load/env resolution, keypair generation) is being deleted, so the whole suite is replaced by tests for the two pure functions in compose.py plus the path helpers.

Cover:
- compose_args with and without an override file present, and with and without a config-dir .env, asserting flag order (base -f before override -f)
- interpolation_env: PADDOCK_AUTHORIZED_KEYS always set; PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT set only with a *.crt present; a non-.crt file in certs/ does not trigger it; PADDOCK_TOOLS_REFRESH set only when refreshing; user-set PADDOCK_SSH_PORT passes through untouched
- paths helpers against a tmp_path XDG_CONFIG_HOME
- the preflight authorized_keys check, both directions

Update tests/conftest.py: it keeps the XDG_CONFIG_HOME redirection and drops XDG_STATE_HOME. Note in AGENTS.md's Testing section that compose.py's runner (like container.py before it) is deliberately not exercised against a real daemon.
acceptance_criteria:
- `uv run pytest` passes with no test importing pydantic, yaml, or ssh
- No test invokes docker

title: Preflight checks: docker, the compose plugin, and authorized_keys
description:
Fail early with actionable messages instead of letting docker produce something confusing.

- docker on PATH (REQUIRED_EXECUTABLES, now just docker), plus a check that the compose plugin is actually present (`docker compose version`) — docker without the v2 plugin is a plausible state on a machine that only ever used docker-compose v1, and the resulting error otherwise reads as 'unknown command'.
- For commands that start the container (up, start, restart, and build since it shares the compose file): ~/.config/paddock/authorized_keys must exist and be a regular file. If it is missing, error with the exact remedy — get the pubkey (`ssh-add -L` if keys live in an agent rather than on disk) and write it to that path. This check matters specifically because Docker would otherwise create a *directory* at the mount source and the container would come up with sshd running and no usable key, which is a slow thing to diagnose.
- Warn (not fail) if certs/ exists but contains no *.crt, since that combination usually means a cert was dropped in with the wrong extension.

All of these produce the same red `error:`/`warning:` output shape as the rest of the CLI.
acceptance_criteria:
- Missing authorized_keys blocks up/start/restart/build with a message naming the path and `ssh-add -L`
- down/stop/status/logs still work with no authorized_keys present
- Missing compose plugin produces a paddock-authored error, not a raw docker one

title: Vendor entrypoint.sh with the /etc/ssh volume workaround
description:
src/paddock/image/entrypoint.sh keeps paddock's current version rather than agent-container's, and only needs path renames.

Must retain:
- mkdir /run/sshd and ssh-keygen -A (no systemd/tmpfiles in the container)
- the copy of /etc/paddock/sshd_config into /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/paddock.conf on every start — this is the workaround for /etc/ssh being a named volume whose stale content would otherwise shadow the image's config forever
- the authorized_keys copy out of the read-only mount into ~/.ssh with correct ownership/perms (the mount is owned by whatever UID it has on the host, which fails sshd's StrictModes)
- exec sshd -D -e under tini

Change: the read-only mount path is /run/paddock/authorized_keys (agent-container used /run/agent-container/).
acceptance_criteria:
- Container starts, sshd_config.d/paddock.conf present and current after an image rebuild against a pre-existing sshd_host_keys volume
- authorized_keys lands as agent:agent 0600
- A key listed in the config-dir authorized_keys can log in

title: Vendor sshd_config and drop PermitUserEnvironment
description:
src/paddock/image/sshd_config keeps agent-container's directives (PermitRootLogin no, AllowUsers agent, no password/kbd-interactive auth, pubkey yes, no X11, AllowAgentForwarding yes, PrintMotd no).

Remove `PermitUserEnvironment yes`. paddock 2.x needed it so it could push settings.yaml env changes into new ssh sessions by writing ~/.ssh/environment via docker exec. settings.yaml is gone, nothing writes that file anymore, and PermitUserEnvironment is a real privilege-escalation surface (a writable ~/.ssh/environment can set LD_PRELOAD for the session) that should not be left on with no feature behind it.
acceptance_criteria:
- sshd_config contains no PermitUserEnvironment line
- Pubkey login as agent works; root login and password auth are refused

title: Ship the empty default CA build context and verify wheel packaging
description:
Add src/paddock/image/ca-certificates/.gitkeep so the compose file's `${PADDOCK_CA_CONTEXT:-./ca-certificates}` default always resolves to a real (empty) directory, making an off-corp-network build a no-op. update-ca-certificates only considers *.crt, so a stray .gitkeep landing in the trust dir is harmless.

Then verify the packaging story, which is the part most likely to silently break: hatchling's wheel target is configured with `packages = ["src/paddock"]`, and the image/ tree is data, not Python. Build a wheel, install it into a throwaway venv, and confirm Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, entrypoint.sh, sshd_config, and ca-certificates/.gitkeep are all present in site-packages/paddock/image/ with the entrypoint still executable. Add explicit hatch build config (force-include or artifacts) if any of it is missing.

Also confirm the installed layout is what a `uv tool install git+https://...` user gets, not just an editable `uv sync` checkout, since the editable case can mask missing package data entirely.
acceptance_criteria:
- `uv build` then install into a scratch venv: all five image/ files present in site-packages
- entrypoint.sh is mode 0755 after install (or the image build chmods it, which the Dockerfile already does)
- `docker compose -f <site-packages path>/image/docker-compose.yml config` renders from the installed copy

title: Document the compose-based paddock and cover migration
description: Rewrite the user-facing and agent-facing docs for what paddock becomes: a compose wrapper with no opinion about how you connect. Cover the config directory contract, the PADDOCK_* interpolation variables, the override-compose layering, and how to migrate off both the old agent-container stack and paddock 2.x without losing the agent_home volume.
acceptance_criteria:
- README describes the config dir, every PADDOCK_* variable, override-compose examples, and says nothing about herdr attach being paddock's job
- AGENTS.md's Architecture/Testing/Commands sections match the new module layout
- A migration section covers reusing an existing agent_home volume and cleaning up the old container/image/volumes
- Version bumped, quality gates green

title: Retire the agent-container repo (out-of-tree follow-up)
description:
Tracked here for completeness, but the change lands in a different repository: /home/agent/code/github.com/kris-steinhoff/agent-container.

Once paddock's vendored image is working, agent-container's Dockerfile is no longer the source of truth. Point its README at paddock (with a short note that the image now ships inside the paddock package and is managed by the paddock CLI) and archive the repo. Leaving it live and unmarked is the failure mode worth avoiding — the next Dockerfile edit would go to the wrong copy, and nothing would tell you.
acceptance_criteria:
- agent-container README points at paddock
- Repo archived, or a deliberate decision recorded not to

title: Optional: paddock init to scaffold the config directory
description:
Nice-to-have, not required by anything else. `paddock init` creates ~/.config/paddock/ with certs/, an authorized_keys stub (or, with an explicit flag, populated from a given pubkey path), and a commented docker-compose.override.yml showing the two things overrides are actually for: bind-mounting a project into /home/agent/workspace/, and adding env or env_file entries.

Must not clobber existing files — write only what is missing, and report what it did. Scope it deliberately small: this scaffolds, it does not manage or migrate config.
acceptance_criteria:
- Run twice, second run changes nothing and says so
- The generated override file is valid input to `docker compose config` when layered
